From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Tom — copying the technical details below and attaching the formal export spec. High-level summary first:

- Retention tiers (hosted):
  • Default: 90 days for full request-level traces (raw events).
  • Standard extended: 180 days (available as add-on).
  • Long-term: 365 days (requires Dedicated/Private deployment or a retention add-on contract for hosted).
  • Archive: we can produce a point-in-time export beyond 365 days if the data is still present in our cold store; that requires 7 business days notice and possible sequencing fees.

- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) for event-level exports; compressed tarball (gz) with an evidence-manifest.json that lists file checksums (sha256) and byte counts. We also support syslog streaming to a customer-managed endpoint for continuous handover (RFC5424).

- Delivery options:
  • S3 presigned upload (preferred): we provide per-file presigned PUT URLs and an evidence manifest. Files are uploaded directly to your bucket.
  • Secure SFTP agent (for customers that prefer push).
  • Encrypted rsync over SSH (by prior arrangement).

- Integrity and attestation: all exports include an evidence-manifest.json (example attached) plus sha256 checksums. For legal attestation we can provide a signed delivery receipt including export start/end timestamps and a hash of the manifest.

- PII/data residency notes: if the tenant has EU residency constraints we will run the EU export playbook — export assets will be routed through our EU staging region and transferred only to EU-hosted buckets unless you request cross-border transfer.

Timeline estimate (assuming tenant ID & snapshot window provided today):
  Day 0 (receive confirmation): scope confirmed, export job scheduled.
  Day 1–2: snapshot + generate NDJSON slices (parallelized).
  Day 3: post-processing, manifest generation, internal QA.
  Day 4: deliver presigned URLs and public-key-signed manifest for upload.
  Day 5: customer completes download; we provide signed delivery receipt.

So hitting end-of-next-week (within 5 business days) is feasible for a single-tenant point-in-time export. For multi-tenant or EU-handled exports add 1–2 days for approvals.

Attachment: audit-export-spec-v2.pdf (contains file layout, manifest schema, example commands).

Let me know the tenant ID and exact from/to timestamps and we'll kick this off.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Delivery
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Quick note on SLA and deletion:

- Hosted tenant retention is enforced by our retention controller. When you request deletion or when retention expires, events are tombstoned and scrubbed from hot storage; full physical deletion from cold snapshots may take up to 30 days depending on compaction schedules. We provide a deletion-attestation report if required.
- If BrightFin needs continuous streaming to an external SIEM, we recommend configuring the syslog endpoint + prefix caching; that avoids snapshot exports for long-term retention.
- Cost implications: point-in-time exports are billed based on compressed GB transferred + a fixed per-export job fee (see export spec). I'll ask billing to provide an estimate once you confirm expected GB.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to sign off the timeline.

— Jonas
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference
